reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 15 excludes indirect damages and carves out Sections 13/14 but contains no monetary cap at all, so it fails the fallback's material term (mutual cap of 12 months' fees) and leaves Customer's direct-damages exposure unlimited.

Redline reaches the preferred position with an additive edit: it appends a mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by Sparkling and USD 1,000,000), defines Excluded Claims preserving the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs while adding indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirms fee obligations are not 'damages'.

Existing sentences (exclusive remedy, indirect-damages exclusion, risk-allocation recital) are retained; the high changed-character ratio reflects necessary insertion of cap and carve-out language rather than an unnecessary rewrite, and the replacement of the final carve-out sentence preserves the original Section 13/14 protection.

Comment is accurate, correctly identifies the gap, states the playbook cap and confirms which obligations sit outside the cap; it does not overstate the clause or misattribute the missing indemnity (correctly deferred to the indemnity rule).
